title: backup-container — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for the MYB1 .myne-backup whole-vault backup container (MYND-254; codec landed MYND-217): the deterministic write side (write_container), the credential-free 5-stage verifier (read_and_verify_container, stages 1–4 — the embedded vault.meta structural parse is the restore engine's stage 5 and is NOT covered here), and the §9.11.3 closed-allowlist path classifier. The container is an UNKEYED integrity layer: per-member SHA-256 over path_len_be16 || path || member_bytes detects accidental corruption, never tampering (tamper defense = the members' own AEAD). Member content is opaque at this layer. Four case kinds: 'encode' (member set → container bytes; input order deliberately unsorted — the writer sorts by raw path bytes), 'verify_ok' (container bytes → verified record triples), 'verify_fail' (one per vectorable BackupContainerError variant), 'classify_path' (§9.11.3 grammar, accept + reject directions). The Rust reference implementation lives at src-tauri/src/backup_container.rs (main myne repository, package myne-desktop — the first vector family whose reference implementation is OUTSIDE the protocol crate; the codec is std/fs-bound by design); spec contract is docs/spec/protocol.md §9.11.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'backup-container/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encode — pin the deterministic member-set → container-bytes mapping

input_members.description: Member set as (path, bytes) pairs, in DELIBERATELY arbitrary order — the writer MUST sort records by raw path bytes (§9.11.2), so the same member set always encodes to identical container bytes regardless of input order.

path.description: Vault-relative member path (must satisfy the §9.11.2 path rules and the §9.11.3 closed allowlist).

bytes_hex.description: Member body bytes (hex), opaque ciphertext stand-ins — the container never parses member content.

expected_container_hex.description: Full container bytes (22-byte header + member table + concatenated member data in table order), hex-encoded lowercase. Producers compare byte-equal — §9.11.2 canonical encoding.

oneOf.title: verify_ok — pin the verifier's parsed record triples

expected_member_records.description: Verified member records in table (= canonical lexicographic) order. The sha256_hex values are independently checkable: SHA-256(path_len_be16 || path || member_bytes), §9.11.2.

oneOf.title: verify_fail — pin a credential-free structural/integrity reject

input_container_hex.description: A malformed/damaged container (hex), empty allowed. The verifier rejects credential-free, BEFORE any disk placement (§9.11.6).

expected_error.description: The specific reject the verifier MUST surface (Rust reference: BackupContainerError, minus the runtime-only Cancelled/Io variants). The §9.11.6 stage order is load-bearing: header checks, then ceilings, THEN the file-length equation, then table parse, then per-member hashes — the two ceiling cases (member_count_overflow / member_table_overflow) are 22-byte header-only files that a wrong-order port would mislabel lengths_inconsistent.

input_member_path.description: A candidate member path (plain string, not hex). The classifier composes the §9.11.2 path rules with the §9.11.3 closed allowlist.

expected_family.description: The §9.11.3 family the path classifies into, or 'rejected' when the path is outside the closed allowlist (writers MUST NOT include it; readers MUST reject it). The grammar is strict: lowercase-hyphenated 36-char disk UUIDs, exactly-64-lowercase-hex attachment ids, '__' snapshot pair separator, exact '.myn' suffix.
